Nine geographically distinct photographs are not automatically nine useful SfM viewpoints; they become reconstruction-grade only after the shared-feature and camera-solve test succeeds. definition.A: reconstruction-grade multi-view source: several views of the same surfaces, with enough baseline and metadata to feed SfM / bundle adjustment
definition.B: single-view facade / sign appearance evidence: colour, sign layout, materials, equipment. Load-bearing for how the corridor LOOKS. Not SfM input.
definition.C: visual acceptance / reference only: in the surveyed radius but not depicting the corridor's facades

retention.rule: at most six class-B/C images, and only on an explicitly open licence, into the scratchpad only
retention.visual_verification: all six were opened and inspected. They show: the entrance ref=1 facade (pale grey ribbed siding, corrugated roof, white 沼部駅 sign with the red Tokyu mark and a blue TM-02 badge), the entrance ref=2 canopy, the ticket gate hall from both sides, the 2006 state of the Tamagawa-side gate sign, and the 多摩堤通り street approach with the level crossing.

mapillary_evidence_phrasing: The two in-AOI OSM mapillary= ids are evidence that Mapillary imagery was ASSOCIATED with features in this AOI during 2022 surveys. That is not proof the images are presently retrievable, nor proof of current coverage.
metadata_only: Coverage discovery only. No provider's imagery was bulk-downloaded. The only bytes fetched are six explicitly open-licensed Wikimedia Commons probe images, held in the session scratchpad and NOT in this bundle.

coverage_is_not_zero.reading: Two OSM surveyors cited Mapillary images at this station in 2022 as the source for footway geometry and surface. That is source-backed evidence that Mapillary holds imagery at the entrance. It is NOT a measurement of density, date coverage or viewpoint multiplicity, which stay UNKNOWN until a token is used.

documented_reason.conclusion: There is no no-token route to Mapillary coverage discovery. This is a documented access rule, not an endpoint mistake.
documented_reason.quote: All requests against https://graph.mapillary.com and https://tiles.mapillary.com must be authorized. They require a client or user access tokens.

steps: 1. Sign in to Mapillary at https://www.mapillary.com/ (a Mapillary account; Facebook sign-in also works).
3. Click 'Register Application'. Name it (for example 'asciicker-Y9-2 FL-4810 coverage probe').
4. Grant ONLY the 'read' scope. Mapillary defines three scopes - read, write, upload - and coverage discovery needs read alone. Do not grant write or upload.

5. Open the registered application and copy its CLIENT TOKEN (format 'MLY|<app_id>|<client_token>'). A client token, not a user OAuth token, is sufficient for both graph.mapillary.com and tiles.mapillary.com.

6. Hand the token over as an environment variable, then re-run: set providers.mapillary.access_token in the probe spec and run scripts/pipeline/street_imagery_probe.py again. No other account action is needed.
exact_operator_action_required.why: every no-token route above was tried and refused; the API documentation states authorization is mandatory

state_tokens.ABSENT_IN_SURVEYED_RADIUS: every queried radius answered and all returned zero, with a control query that returned pictures
state_tokens.PRESENT: at least one picture was returned and is recorded
state_tokens.UNKNOWN_PENDING_ACCESS: the provider answered with a credential refusal; coverage is undetermined, NOT zero

supersedes.what_still_stands: The Panoramax result is re-run here and reproduces exactly: zero pictures at 100, 250, 500 and 1000 m on both queried instances, against a Paris control that returned 1000.
supersedes.what_was_wrong: v1 surveyed Panoramax only and concluded 'Corridor is NOT reconstructable from open street-level imagery today'. That sentence generalised one provider's zero to every provider. KartaView was never queried; Mapillary and Google Street View answered with credential refusals, which is UNKNOWN coverage, not zero coverage; Wikimedia Commons and other open photo pools were never searched.

tool.note: The prober is provider-agnostic and carries no Numabe constants. The AOI, the entrance node and the radius ladder arrive through the spec.

verdict: Open street-level CAPTURE-PLATFORM coverage of the corridor is absent on Panoramax (ABSENT_IN_SURVEYED_RADIUS, control 1000) and absent inside the AOI on KartaView (PRESENT regionally, nearest capture 417.0 m away, control 890). Mapillary and Google Street View are UNKNOWN_PENDING_ACCESS: both refused every no-token route, including at the control location, so neither zero is established - and two OSM footways inside the AOI cite Mapillary image ids from 2022 surveys. Open PHOTOGRAPHIC coverage of the corridor is PRESENT and substantial: 15 openly licensed Wikimedia Commons images lie inside the AOI polygon, the nearest 4.9 m from the selected entrance, including a nine-frame CC-BY-4.0 single-session walk with compass headings that satisfies both the >=2 and >=3 viewpoint tests. The v1 sentence 'this corridor is not reconstructable from open street-level imagery today' is withdrawn: it was never tested against KartaView, Mapillary, Google or any open photo pool.
